for a wide class of distributions the moments of the queue length are bounded by a constant times the moments of the unused service capacity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found simple and sharp bounds for all moments of the stationary queue lengths in the bulk service queueing system.

we prove that the mean queue length of a discrete-time bulk-service queueing model with Poisson input is bounded by 2, and we provide an explicit expression for this upper bound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the moment series of a stationary queue length can often be represented as a moment of a random variable related to the unused capacity.
the bounds on the moment generating function of the stationary queue size are tight in the sense that the ratio of the upper bound to the lower bound tends to one as the service capacity increases.
the mean and variance of stationary queue length can often be bounded in a simple and intuitive manner, without having to solve a complex system of equations.
